  3. How the tests run, and how to go fast

#How the tests run, and how to go fast

tools\test_all.ps1 runs every test of the project, step by step. This page says what it does with your time, how to ask for less of it while you work, which tools tell you where the time goes, and how to write an end-to-end test.

#The commands of a working day

What you wantCommand
Everything a commit should pass (nothing runs twice: see below)tools\test_all.ps1 -Quick
The same, every step really runtools\test_all.ps1 -Quick -NoCache
Only what depends on what you changed since mastertools\test_all.ps1 -Quick -Changed
One step, or a family of themtools\test_all.ps1 -Quick -Only 'unit tests: (url|http)$'
What failed in the last runtools\test_all.ps1 -Quick -Failed
The names of the steps, and how many files each depends ontools\test_all.ps1 -Quick -List
Where the time of a run goestools\test_all.ps1 -Quick -Profile
What the CI runs (with test262 as a job of its own, and tools\asan.ps1)tools\test_all.ps1 -CI -NoAsan
The full runtools\test_all.ps1

Run them with powershell -NoProfile -File. A step that -Only, -Failed or -Changed chooses brings with it the steps that build what it uses (build\policytest.exe, build\e2e.wasm). They all say at the end how many steps they left out: they are for your loop, never instead of the CI's run.

#The end of a run

A run ends with the slowest steps, how many Wren processes the scripts started, how long they spent in fixed waits (Start-Sleep, by script), and then what matters:

steps: 2 FAIL, 1 FLAKY, 89 PASS, 20 CACHED; 5967 checks counted
FAIL unit tests: httpcache
  log: S:\...\build\test_logs\unit_tests_httpcache.log
  again: powershell -NoProfile -File tools\test_all.ps1 -Quick -NoCache -Only 'unit\ tests:\ httpcache'
  only the failed tests: add -define:ODIN_TEST_NAMES=httpcache.test_disk_damage to its odin test
  - httpcache.test_disk_damage   expected ...

The same is left in build\: test_report.txt (that text), test_steps.tsv (every step's status, seconds and number of checks: compare two of them to see that a change lost nothing), test_failed.txt (what -Failed reads), test_logs\ (the whole output of each step that did not pass), test_all_times.txt (durations, the order of the next run).

#What runs, in what order

The run happens on a Windows desktop of its own (tools/test_desktop.ps1): no step can take the focus, the mouse or the keyboard of the person at the machine, and their clicks reach no step. -Ui stays on the real desktop, its steps need the real input.

Every step is a process of its own; -Jobs of them run at a time (three per four processors, at most 12; two with -CI), longest first by the durations of the last run. A step marked -Light mostly waits and takes no slot, up to -LightJobs of them (4; 2 with -CI). Each step that talks to the test server has a server of its own on a block of ports of its own, so several worktrees test side by side. What a step builds comes first (the steps named build *). -Perf and -Ui add the steps that depend on the machine's speed or on a desktop (CONTRIBUTING); a full run adds the check build, the AddressSanitizer unit tests, the whole of WPT and test262, the network stress.

#The result cache

With -Quick on a developer's machine, a step that has passed with exactly the same inputs says CACHED and does not run again (tools\test_cache.ps1, results in build\test_cache\). That is what makes the second run of the day short: a change in src/url reruns the packages that import url, and the steps that use the browser.

A result is found by content, never by time. Its key is the SHA-256 of:

  • the version Odin says it is, the run's flags (-Quick, -CI, -Ui, the time factor), the step's name and text, and the values of its variables (flags of the compile included);
  • for a step that compiles and runs Odin packages: every file of those packages and of everything they import (wb:, toolkit:, web:, relative imports, parsed from the sources, for every build tag), what they #load, the libraries they link, the paths written in their strings ("tools/build_js.ps1", "examples/site/images/%s": what a test reads while it runs), examples\, assets\, api\, sdk\, the test server, the native libraries;
  • for a step that runs a script or the browser: the whole tree (src, ext\gui_toolkit, tools, wpt, native, api, sdk, examples, assets, build.bat, odin.version, the libraries), tests of packages aside;
  • for what is about the documentation or the changelog, what generates files (odin run), the licence Worker: all of that and docs, site, changelog.d, licence.

What cannot be resolved (a path with a variable in it, an unknown collection) takes the whole tree: an input too many costs a rerun, one too few could hide a failure. tools\test_cache_test.ps1, itself a step, compares the packages found with the compiler's own import graph (-show-import-graph) and checks that a change of each kind of input changes a key, and that a change of something else does not.

Only a pass is kept, and only if the key computed when the step has ended is the one it started with: a file edited during the step leaves no result. A result of a step that built a program stands only while that program is on the disk as the step left it. A result lasts 7 days: what no file says (a certificate that expires, a date) gets its chance.

What a cache cannot see: a test that passes one time in two has passed. That is the price, and why:

  • the CI never takes a result on master (a pull request does: .github/workflows/ci.yml, by that pull request's earlier runs);
  • a full run, -Perf and -NoCache take none; WREN_TEST_CACHE=0 is -NoCache for a whole session.

#The shared code of test processes

The JavaScript engine's image compiles in 5 s of CPU, once in each process, and a run starts hundreds of them, each without a profile or with a throwaway one. tools\test_env.ps1 sets WREN_TEST_WASM_CACHE to build\wasm_cache: all the test processes then read the disk cache of the engine (src/wasm/module_cache.odin: keyed by the image and the engine's configuration, authenticated), 0.2 s of CPU instead of 5. The tests of that cache itself (wasm.disk_cache) keep their own. A release ignores the variable. -NoCache turns this off too.

#WPT

A run of WPT spent 58 % of its time on tests that time out (1300 of 8800, 50 of them for 60 s): a test expected to time out waits for what will not come, and the page of a test that can do nothing more is given a second to prove it.

With -Quick, and tools\wpt.ps1 -FastTimeouts for a whole run:

  • a test the expectations say times out gets 3 s (-timeout-cap), a page that can do nothing more 300 ms (-idle);
  • all that fails then goes through the second chance: run again together, without either, with 4 times the limit and the engine's limit on one script out of the way, and what still fails alone. Only a test that regresses there counts.

So a shorter limit can cost a rerun, not hide a regression. What it does not see is a test that has begun to pass: a whole run without it does, and -Update (which refuses the cap) records it. -Only keeps the whole limits too: someone is looking at that test. -NoFastTimeouts turns it off under -Quick.

#Writing an end-to-end test

An end-to-end test is an Odin @(test) procedure of src/tools/e2e, on Odin's own test runner. It calls the browser directly: the program links package browser, the browser runs in the test's thread and process, and a barrier runs its loop, turn by turn, until what it waits for holds. There is no window of the system, no channel, no JSON, no other thread to wait for: the frames are the real renderer's, offscreen, made as fast as they are asked for, and nothing can take the focus, the mouse or the keyboard of whoever is at the machine.

Odin
package e2e_scenarios

import "core:testing"
import "wb:e2e"

@(test)
the_title_shows :: proc(t: ^testing.T) {
	server := e2e.test_server(t)
	s := e2e.start(t, {size = {1280, 800}})
	e2e.navigate(s, e2e.url(server, "/site/about.html"))   // returns once loaded
	testing.expect_value(t, e2e.eval(s, "document.title"), "About")
	e2e.key(s, "Ctrl+L")
	e2e.type_text(s, "hello")
	e2e.wait_js(s, "document.readyState == 'complete'")
	c := e2e.pixel(e2e.capture(s, {target = .Page}), 10, 10)   // the next frame's pixels
	testing.expect(t, c.a == 255)
}

The rules:

  • One file per subject, src/tools/e2e/<name>.odin, with its checks kept as they mean. A file's tests are one step of test_all: Step '...' { Invoke-WrenE2E 'build\e2e_test.exe' '<name>' }, with its marks (-UiOnly, -NoCI, -Weight). Invoke-WrenE2E finds the tests in the file.
  • An action that fails ends the test there, saying where it was called from, what failed and the folder of what it left (build/e2e/<test>/: failure.png, failure_console.txt, the test's own e2e.shots, kept only when it failed). So a scenario checks no return. Checks are testing.expect*: they go on.
  • Barriers, never sleeps. wait_load, wait_frames(s, n), wait_selector, wait_js(s, condition), wait_chrome_still (the interface's animations have ended), wait_until(s, ready_proc, "what") and wait_until(s, data, ready_proc, "what"). Each has deadline := DEFAULT_DEADLINE, which only ends a failing run. Wait for the state itself, not for a number of frames: wait_frames is for what is done within a frame or two by construction.
  • The browser's animations go by frames (control_begin: each frame is one of the usual length for them, however fast it is made), so a 500 ms animation is 30 frames. What a page does on a real timer is still real time: the preference that shortens it (forms.caret.blink_ms) rather than a wait for it.
  • Something the browser does not let you see or do: add it to the browser, not to the test. A typed procedure in src/browser/control.odin, which the remote method (remote_methods.odin, only the JSON's decoding there) calls too; a field of api.Stats, filled by control_stats. Then the wrapper in src/e2e/e2e.odin.
  • One browser at a time in a process (the browser's state is the process's), and e2e.start ends with the test, as do its profile (e2e.temp_profile(t) for one that e2e.restart must find again), e2e.temp_folder(t) and e2e.test_server(t). The tests of one run go one after the other (ODIN_TEST_THREADS=1); test_all runs one process per file, side by side.
  • Only what is about a process starts one: a launch, an exit code, a crash, a second start, the console launcher, the channel itself. e2e.launch(t, {...}) gives a Wren of its own, over the channel, with the typed client wb:remote/api (api.navigate(p.s, url)), e2e.quit(p) its exit code, e2e.kill(p) a crash. It is headless too unless hidden = true; start holds its environment, its folder, its outputs. Any other program is e2e.program (e2e.run to its end: its exit code and what it printed). What another process does to the disk is waited for with e2e.wait_file, e2e.wait_gone, e2e.wait_for. A hidden window needs a desktop nobody uses: test_all's, or by hand tools\test_desktop.ps1 -Command "...".
  • What is about the window of the system runs on a real one, never shown: e2e.start(t, {hidden = true}), in the test's process, so that the window procedure is called on the test's thread as the system calls it. src/tools/e2e/real_window.odin is that core (WM_DPICHANGED, WM_NCHITTEST, WM_SETCURSOR, the z-order for a drop, the swap chain), frame_gate.odin and devtools_resize.odin use it too; e2e.launch(t, {hidden = true}) when something else must read it from outside (a11y_uia.odin). It needs a desktop session: test_all's own, tools\test_desktop.ps1 -Command "build\e2e_test.exe -tests:name" by hand. What needs a paint or the system's frame goes through show_unseen (window_native.odin): shown where nobody sees nor touches it.
  • Nothing left allocated: build\e2e_test_check.exe is the same program built with -define:WREN_TRACK_MEMORY=true (full runs: every allocation of the process goes through the tracker of base). When a test's browser has ended and the test has let go of what it holds, whatever is still allocated, or was freed twice, is listed and fails the test (end_of_test). Only scenarios about what a session holds (workers, service workers, file systems, the back/forward cache, partitions) run there: a step of test_all says which.

Running them by hand: build\e2e_test.exe -tests:the_title_shows (no window opens, no other desktop is needed, except for a scenario with hidden = true), or test_all -Quick -NoCache -Only 'src.tools.e2e'. WREN_E2E_TRACE=1 prints every call with its time, WREN_PHASES=1 the phases of a start and an end of the browser (a real wren.exe says them too).

Two things core:testing does not give: a test stopped by a signal (testing.fail_now, a panic) can happen once per run on Windows, the runner lets go of a lock it does not hold, and the next signal waits for ever; e2e stops its tests through a limit of 0 instead (hence the "Test timed out" after a failure's message). And checks that pass say nothing: test_all counts tests here, not checks.

#Writing a test that is quick

The rules are in CONTRIBUTING: wait for a condition, with a limit that only ends a failing run (the barriers above, wren ctl wait for a script, Invoke-WrenBuildIfStale, Ensure-WrenBuild), one shared Wren between scenarios. And check what a wait returns: a tool that waited for a line nobody logs (jsloadtest) spent its 120 s limit in every run, and passed.

#Virtual time

host.Loop reads its time through host.now_ns. A test gives the loop a host.Virtual_Clock (clock_virtual) and moves it: clock_advance(&loop, d) runs at once what falls due on the way, each timer at its own deadline; clock_move only moves it, as a stalled machine would. loop_wait on such a clock does not wait for a timer. Production pays one test of a pointer.

A test does not sleep to wait for another thread: it waits on the state (a semaphore, a completion posted to the loop, base.await when the code under test has no signal). The few real sleeps left in unit tests measure the real clock, and say so.

#The test programs and their pages

jswebtest and jsdomtest are test programs of core:testing: one @(test) per section (build\jswebtest.exe -tests:core,webgl_process, or tools\jsweb_run.ps1 core webgl_process with a test server). They run one test at a time (-define:ODIN_TEST_THREADS=1) and share one loop: what the process keeps (image cache, stores) binds to the first loop it sees. A last test, zz_the_process_ends_with_nothing_left, undoes it all and checks the leaks.

A page's script talks to its program through the functions of wrenTest (api/testhost.widl, native/js/odin/test_host.odin, src/page/test_host.odin, src/tools/testhost), which exists only in a page given a test host: testBegin, testEnd, check, measure, note, signal, skip, done. The console is no protocol any more. testhost.finish fails:

  • a section that ran another number of tests than the one its @(test) declares (tests = 8), or none, or fewer checks than it declares (min_checks);
  • a section whose script never said done(), a test that checked nothing;
  • a skip("webgl-adapter" | "av1-decoder", why) that the program does not find true of the machine: it makes a context of its own for the first (only "no graphics adapter" from the GPU process counts as none), asks the media backend for the second.

A true skip prints SKIP [section] ..., is counted, and test_all lists it at the end of a run.

#Debugging the tests' time

  • tools\test_profile.ps1 -Out build\prof\x -Run "<command>" (or test_all -Profile): every process of the tree, by program, count, wall and CPU seconds; the use of the processors second by second, the tree's and the rest of the machine's. -Compare a -With b compares two runs; build\prof\x.processes.tsv has each process and its command line. Read the CPU seconds when other runs share the machine: they barely move, the wall clock does.
  • WREN_SLEEPS_FILE, set by test_all: the fixed waits of the scripts, by script.
  • WREN_STARTS_FILE, set by test_all: the Wren processes they start.
  • wren ctl wait load|idle|stable|quiet|selector|function|frames, wren ctl stats, wren ctl reset, wren ctl checkpoint: Remote control.
  • A step that fails under load and passes alone is marked -Flaky: it says what failed, and fails nothing.
